bugs.additionalRegression: Reusing an old invited nickname for another account previously revoked the first account invitation, rather than addressing the current nickname account.
bugs.rootCause: Invitation grant/consume/list are bound to target_user_id, but revocation and list cleanup used mutable nicknames.
bugs.fix: Resolve recipient from authenticated current sessions, registered nickname ownership, or trusted persisted same-channel invitation; revoke account-bound channel and session-list rows while preserving issuer checks, other recipients and current-nickname precedence.

limitations: routeBehavior.alias uses the discovered route alias template expected by current reporter; requestPath preserves the concrete request, including encoded channel and query. README describes alias differently; coordinator notified.

33 executable tests exercise 31 CHAN IDs; CHAN-033 has additional NOT IMPLEMENTED lifecycle disposition because positive archived-name reuse is unavailable; this is not a claim to cover the entire 339-scenario matrix. Missing required evidence dimensions are marked PARTIAL in the per-ID ledger even when the bounded test passes.

REST JOIN/membership creation is absent: CHAN-022/023 are NOT IMPLEMENTED, never passing route-not-found tests. Administrative changes to restrictions are explicitly privileged controls, not REST JOIN parity.

All twelve requested channel names/configurations are created across isolated cases. #restricted uses implemented registered-account +R; a separate arbitrary registered-channel access policy is not exposed. Custom role inheritance/hierarchy policy remains outside this membership slice and is not assumed available.

Destructive deletion reserves archived names, including with purged messages; reusing such a name is unavailable. The CHAN-033 test verifies the actual documented archive/reservation policy; whether acceptance requires name reuse needs product review.
Chronologically distinct #history messages use real creation times; this slice does not simulate weeks/months of history or retention.

Event assertions use actual ws clients and authorized positive controls with IRC PING barriers plus an 80ms local waitUntil delivery drain; this establishes bounded local workerd output, not distributed exactly-once delivery or production hibernation.
Secret attachment read checks use the real SQLite media provider; R2-specific and media lifecycle coverage belongs to the separate media slice.
Invitation expiry uses a publicly created invitation aged in stopped SQLite and a new runtime; it does not wait through 24 real hours.
Account bans intentionally pair banned Bob with unbanned and matching-exception controls; the full network/account-role matrix and disabled/expired identity lifecycle belongs to other slices.
